test_focus: expand engineering-craft seed library from 15 (Phase 15) to 30 entries. Pure curation — no LLM cost, no experiment. Reduces seed-repetition for daily-dreaming engineers.
tester: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context), live as the developer

new_seeds_themes: metric self-reference and observability blind spots
drift over years (encoding bugs, timezone drift, deprecated APIs)
merge resolutions that ship and never surface

examples_added: The shared dictionary mutated in five threads that worked for three years because nobody held it long.
The race condition that only appeared when the engineer who knew about it was on vacation.
The 'temporary' shell script in /opt that ran every five minutes for the entire life of the company.
The connection pool that never grew because the metric measuring its size was itself in the pool.
The merge that resolved a conflict by deleting both sides, ship-tested for six weeks, never noticed.
The performance fix that was a regression in disguise because the slow path had been suppressing a bug.
rationale: Phase 15 validated the engineering-craft category at 15 entries. At one dream every ~30 min (production cadence), an engineer would cycle through all 15 in 7.5 hours — fast enough that seed repetition becomes noticeable within a single day. Doubling to 30 doubles the cycle time and reduces the chance of two consecutive same-seed dreams. The new entries follow the same texture (the bug live for years, the system holding hidden context) so the Phase 15 effect should generalize.

test_suite_stats.note: test count unchanged; existing TestDreamSeeds tests still pass, floor moved 15→30

feature_verdicts.engineering_craft_seed_library_size: sings — 30 entries, ~2x reduction in same-seed-twice probability per agent-day

known_limitations: 30 entries may still be tight for an agent that runs for weeks. Future phases could expand toward 50-75 entries if observability shows seed repetition is hurting variety.
verdict: READY TO MERGE — pure curation work, no behavior change beyond reducing repetition.
next_steps: Phase 16 (running): does engineering-craft + neutral wrapper beat no-injection control on technical prompts?
Phase 17 (next): per-prompt routing for decision-shaped prompts.
